title: Paid editorial content not made clear (advertorial)
instrument: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
binding_note: Schedule 20 lists commercial practices which are in all circumstances considered unfair (section 225). It applies to traders.

in_force.note: The Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (Commencement No. 2) Regulations 2025 (SI 2025/272), regulation 2(3), bring Chapter 1 of Part 4 into force on 6 April 2025 (except sections 232, 234 and 235). Section 225 and Schedule 20 sit in that Chapter, and the revised XML gives the same start date.

sources.note: Revised text as held on legislation.gov.uk; the XML carries extent E+W+S+N.I. and a start date of 2025-04-06 for paragraphs 12, 13 and 25.

quotes.text: Using editorial content in the media to promote a product where a trader has paid for the promotion without making that clear in the content or by images or sounds clearly identifiable by the consumer.
Chapter 1 (protection from unfair trading) of Part 4 (consumer rights and disputes), except sections 232, 234 and 235.

elements.label: Content presented as editorial or ordinary content is used to promote a product
elements.note: Whether a social media post counts as "editorial content in the media" is a legal question this entry does not settle.

elements.label: A trader paid for the promotion
The payment is not made clear in the content or by images or sounds the consumer can clearly identify

does_not_prove: Daylight Commons cannot see payment for unlabelled posts. A match on visible elements is a comparison with a published definition. It is not a finding by a court, the CMA or a trading standards service, and it says nothing about elements Daylight Commons cannot see.
